{{nihongo|'''Niukawakami Shrine'''|丹生川上神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Niu Kawakami Shrine'' (Niu Kawakami Shrine) is located in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}{{ill|Yoshino District, Nara|Q1154558|qid=Q1154558}}{{ill|Higashiyoshino, Nara|ar|هيغاشيوشينو|ca|Higashi-Yoshino|ceb|HIgashiyoshino Mura|es|Higashiyoshino (Nara)|fa|هیگاشی‌یوشینو، نارا|fr|Higashiyoshino|hy|Հիգասիյոսինո|it|Higashiyoshino|ja|東吉野村|ko|히가시요시노촌|pl|Higashiyoshino|ru|Хигасиёсино|tl|Higashiyoshino, Nara|tr|Higashiyoshino|uk|Хіґасі-Йосіно|ur|ہیگاشی یوشینو، نارا|zh|東吉野村|qid=Q1203148}}. {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), one of the {{ill|Twenty-Two Shrines|Q215320|qid=Q215320}} (Shimohachisha). {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old Shrine Ranking}} is {{ill|Q712534|lt=Kanpei Taisha}}, and currently it is {{ill|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274|qid=Q10898274}} of {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.

=== About the company name ===
In ancient times, it was called ``Amashi Myojin,'' and from {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}} it was also called ``Aritori Myojin.''

After {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}}, Yoshino District{{ill|Kawakami, Nara|Q1204424|qid=Q1204424|lt=Kawakami Village}} {{ill|Niukawakami Upper Shrine|Q10877366|qid=Q10877366}} {{ill|Shimoichi, Nara|Q1203064|qid=Q1203064}} {{ill|Niukawakami Lower Shrine|ja|丹生川上神社下社|zh|丹生川上神社下社|qid=Q10877367}} came to be called ``Nyu Kawakami Shrine Middle Shrine,'' but this was because two shrines, an upper and lower shrine, already existed, so it was called ``middle'', and it does not represent the positional relationship or the rank of the shrine.

Ikari Amaya". </ref>, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amashi}} is an ancient Chinese deity of praying for rain, along with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Fuhaku}}, so this is a divine name that owes its devotion to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tangfu culture}}. It is clear that <ref> ``{{ill|Baopuzi|Q831242|qid=Q831242}}'' also includes ``Tatsuya Amashisha'', and it can be pointed out that he is related to the god of the dragon, who is also the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=dragon and snake god}}. </ref>. In addition, when praying for rain, a black horse was offered, and when the rain stopped, a white horse (or blue horse) was offered, but this was based on the idea that {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=horse}} was seen as a god of water or an animal closely related to water.<ref>{{ill|Ishida Eiichirō|Q6080158|qid=Q6080158}} "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kappa Komahiki ko}}" (1948). </ref>, and the color of the horse is probably {{ill|Sympathetic magic|Q485000|qid=Q485000}} based on the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=ideal association}} of rain clouds and black, and sunny skies and white. In particular, Part 1, Chapter 3, ``Empathy Magic,'' and Chapter 5, ``Magical Control of the Weather,'' collect cases in which black animals are used when praying for rain, and white (or red) animals are used when praying for the rain to stop. === History ===
According to the shrine's legend, the enshrined place is the place where {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}} enshrined Tenjin Jigi upon the instruction of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tenjin}} during his {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Q11590444|qid=Q11590444|lt=Tenjin}} and won the war. This is the place where the fortune-telling was made, as stated in the 9th month of Bogo section of ``{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}'', the pre-enthronement period of Emperor Jimmu, and this is said to be the site of Shikinai Niu Shrine, where {{ill|Uda, Nara|ar|يودا (نارا)|azb|اودا، نارا|ca|Uda (Nara)|ce|Уда (гӀала)|ceb|Uda Shi|de|Uda (Nara)|es|Uda (Nara)|et|Uda (Jaapan)|fa|اودا، نارا|fi|Uda (Nara)|fr|Uda (Nara)|gl|Uda, Nara|hy|Ուդա|id|Uda, Nara|it|Uda (Nara)|ja|宇陀市|ko|우다시|min|Uda, Nara|mzn|اودا، نارا|nl|Uda (stad)|pl|Uda (miasto)|ro|Uda, Nara|ru|Уда (город)|sv|Uda, Nara|tl|Uda, Nara|tr|Uda, Nara|tt|Уда (шәһәр)|uk|Уда (Нара)|ur|ادا، نارا|vi|Uda, Nara|war|Uda, Nara|zh|宇陀市|zh_classical|宇陀市|zh_min_nan|Uda-chhī|zh_yue|宇陀|qid=Q863747}} is the enshrined place of Amashi Haibara. </ref>. Specifically, Jimmu had Heiren and Genren made from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tenkaguyama}} soil submerged in the river, had Shiinetsuya observe the state of river fish, learned that there was a vein of {{ill|Cinnabar|Q104614|qid=Q104614|lt=tan}} (mercury), and decided to worship various gods at 500 masakaki trees and pacify the country.
{{quote|The imperial order says, ``The two of you will reach the heavenly fragrance mountain, take the earth, and be able to come. Whether the basic work is successful or not, it is up to you to predict. Efforts are in order.'' The Emperor's great joy, Nosotori Nyukawa Kaminoyuki, 500 Masaka trees, and the deities enshrined. |Nihonshoki}}{{ill|Hakuhō|ja|白鳳|ru|Хакухо|zh|白鳳|qid=Q11580612}}4 years ({{ill|675|ab|675|af|675|am|675 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|675|ar|675|ary|675|arz|675|ast|675|az|675|azb|۶۷۵ (میلادی)|be|675|be_x_old|675|bg|675|bn|৬৭৫|bpy|মারি ৬৭৫|br|675|bs|675.|ca|675|cdo|675 nièng|ceb|675|ckb|٦٧٥|crh|675|cs|675|cv|675|cy|675|da|675|de|675|el|675|eml|675|eo|675|es|675|et|675|eu|675|fa|۶۷۵ (میلادی)|fi|675|fo|675|fr|675|fy|675|ga|675|gan|675年|gd|675|gl|675|he|675|hi|675|hr|675.|ht|675 (almanak jilyen)|hu|675|hy|675|id|675|io|675|it|675|ja|675年|jv|675|ka|675|kk|675 жыл|ko|675년|la|675|lb|675|lij|675|lmo|675|lt|675 m.|map_bms|675|mdf|675|mg|675|mhr|675|mk|675|mr|इ.स. ६७५|mrj|675 и|ms|675|mzn|۶۷۵|nah|675|nap|675|nds|675|nds_nl|675|new|सन् ६७५|nl|675|nn|675|no|675|nrm|675|nso|675|oc|675|or|୬୭୫|os|675-æм аз|pl|675|pnb|675|pt|675|qu|675|ro|675|ru|675 год|rue|675|sa|६७५|scn|675|sd|675ع|se|675|sh|675.|shn|675|si|675|simple|675|sk|675|sl|675|sq|675|sr|675|su|675|sv|675|sw|675|tg|Соли 675|th|พ.ศ. 1218|tk|675|tl|675|tly|675|tr|675|tt|675 ел|uk|675|ur|675ء|uz|675|vec|675|vi|675|war|675|wuu|675年|xmf|675|zh|675年|zh_min_nan|675 nî|zh_yue|675年|qid=Q30523}}) {{ill|Q81 91796|qid=Q81 91796|lt=The Elephant Goddess}} was enshrined at the site of the current Nyu Shrine on the south bank of the Mitarashi River ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takami River}}, and later moved to its current location. Furthermore, the ``Owa Shrine Notebook'' states that this provision was made because it is a separate shrine to Yamato Shrine. </ref>. In "{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}", it is ranked as {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029|lt=Kanpei Taisha}} (Meishin Taisha), and even when the Ritsuryo system was relaxed, {{j alink|Twenty-two shrines|Q215320}} Although it remained highly respected by the Imperial Court, it gradually declined as the number of offerings it received decreased, and after the Onin War, its whereabouts were finally unknown. In addition, the shrine's legend says that it was frequently rebuilt and renovated after the Middle Ages, and the liangbun of construction in {{ill|Keian|Q1146135|qid=Q1146135}}3 ({{ill|1650|Q6951|qid=Q6951}}), which is in our possession, includes: It is written that a new Nyu Shrine was built on the site of the original enshrinement, and that the head office was renamed ``Aritori Myojin'', following the {{ill|Chinjugami|Q97479976|qid=Q97479976}} of {{ill|Kongōbu-ji|Q1203429|qid=Q1203429}}.Since the early modern period, research on the "Shinmyocho" has become more active, and when the location of Shikinai shrines in particular became an issue, Nyukawakami Shrine Shimosha was first identified as Shikinai Taisha Nyukawakami Shrine, and then {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Meiji}}, Kamisha was identified, but in {{ill|1915|Q2084|qid=Q2084}} ({{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}}4), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Moriguchi Narakichi}} wrote about the Nyukawakami Shrine. '', he researched that this shrine, which had been listed as a {{ill|Q712534|lt=Gosha}} since the Meiji era, was Shikinai Nyukawakami Shrine, and as subsequent research proved this, the company name was changed in 1999. The name was changed from ``Aritori Shrine'' to ``Nyukawakami Shrine,'' and the two shrines above and below were called ``Chusha,'' and the three shrines were collectively called ``Kanpei Taisha Nyukawakami Shrine,'' with the shrine's office being placed at the center of the shrine. With the abolition of the government system after World War II, the three shrines became independent in {{ill|1952|ab|1952|af|1952|als|1952|am|1952 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1952|ar|1952|ary|1952|arz|1952|ast|1952|av|1952|avk|1952|az|1952|azb|۱۹۵۲ (میلادی)|ba|1952 йыл|ban|1952|bar|1952|bat_smg|1952|bcl|1952|be|1952|be_x_old|1952|bg|1952|bh|1952|bjn|1952|bn|১৯৫২|bpy|মারি ১৯৫২|br|1952|bs|1952.|ca|1952|cbk_zam|1952|cdo|1952 nièng|ce|1952 шо|ceb|1952|ckb|١٩٥٢|co|1952|crh|1952|cs|1952|csb|1952|cv|1952|cy|1952|da|1952|de|1952|diq|1952|dsb|1952|el|1952|eml|1952|eo|1952|es|1952|et|1952|eu|1952|fa|۱۹۵۲|fi|1952|fiu_vro|1952|fo|1952|fr|1952|frp|1952|frr|1952|fur|1952|fy|1952|ga|1952|gag|1952|gan|1952年|gcr|1952|gd|1952|gl|1952|gn|1952|gv|1952|hak|1952-ngièn|he|1952|hi|१९५२|hif|1952|hr|1952.|hsb|1952|ht|1952 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1952|hy|1952|hyw|1952 թուական|ia|1952|id|1952|ie|1952|ilo|1952|io|1952|is|1952|it|1952|ja|1952年|jbo|1952moi|jv|1952|ka|1952|kaa|1952|kbp|1952|kk|1952 жыл|kn|೧೯೫೨|ko|1952년|krc|1952 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1952|ku|1952|kv|1952-ӧд во|kw|1952|la|1952|lb|1952|lez|1952 йис|li|1952|lij|1952|lmo|1952|ln|1952|lt|1952 m.|lv|1952. gads|mai|१९५२|map_bms|1952|mdf|1952|mg|1952|mhr|1952|mi|1952|min|1952|mk|1952|ml|1952|mn|1952 он|mr|इ.स. १९५२|mrj|1952 и|ms|1952|my|၁၉၅၂|myv|1952 ие|mzn|۱۹۵۲|nah|1952|nap|1952|nds|1952|nds_nl|1952|new|ई सं १९५२|nl|1952|nn|1952|no|1952|nrm|1952|nso|1952|oc|1952|olo|1952|or|୧୯୫୨|os|1952-æм аз|pa|1952|pam|1952|pap|1952|pl|1952|pnb|1952|pt|1952|qu|1952|ro|1952|roa_tara|1952|ru|1952 год|rue|1952|sah|1952 сыл|sat|᱑᱙᱕᱒|sc|1952|scn|1952|sd|1952ع|se|1952|sh|1952.|shn|1952|si|1952|simple|1952|sk|1952|sl|1952|smn|1952|so|1952|sq|1952|sr|1952|stq|1952|su|1952|sv|1952|sw|1952|szl|1952|ta|1952|te|1952|tg|Соли 1952|th|พ.ศ. 2495|tk|1952|tl|1952|tly|1952|tpi|1952|tr|1952|tt|1952 ел|ty|1952|udm|1952 ар|ug|1952 - === God level ===
In {{ill|Kōnin (era)|Q1373070|qid=Q1373070}}9 ({{ill|818|Q25083|qid=Q25083}}), he was conferred the rank of Jugoinoge (Junior Fifth Rank and Lower Rank) ("{{ill|Nihon Kiryaku|Q1053542|qid=Q1053542}}" quoted in "Shoku Nihongi"), and thereafter {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jowa}} 7th year ({{ill|840|Q29936|qid=Q29936}}) Seigoi 5th rank lower, 10th year 10th year junior fourth rank lower (hereinafter referred to as "Shoku Nihongi"), {{jalink |Kasho|Q1373157}} 3rd year ({{ill|850|Q30364|qid=Q30364}}) Seishiinoge ("{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tales of Emperor Montoku}}"), {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} 1st year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}) Jusanmi, {{jalink|Genkei|Q747451} }In the first year ({{ill|877|Q23905|qid=Q23905}}), he progressed to Seisanmi (the above is ``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}''). By the way, in "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Owa Shrine Notes}}," it is written that he was promoted to Junior Second Rank in Kanpei 9 ({{ill|897|Q30468|qid=Q30468}}).

=== Priest ===
Since the Middle Ages until the {{ill|Azuchi–Momoyama period|Q319531|qid=Q319531}}, {{ill|Ogawa clan|Q135692551|qid=Q135692551}} took over the priesthood, and ``Manizan Daijo-in'' of Kongobu-ji {{ill|matsuji|Q11519671|qid=Q11519671}} served as the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Betto temple}}. The Ogawa clan held both the lordship of this area (Ogawa-go) and the {{ill|shōkan|Q11618914|qid=Q11618914}} of Amashi-sho, Uda District (therefore, they also had jurisdiction over Shikinai Nyu Shrine, which is enshrined in the same sho), and boasted power as the local lord ({{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012|lt=In the Nanbokucho period}}, he belonged to the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kitabatake clan}}, and was also active in the recapture of the Divine Seal ({{ill|Chōroku incident|Q11653526|qid=Q11653526}}) in {{ill|Chōroku|Q1193524|qid=Q1193524}}2 ({{ill|1458|Q6522|qid=Q6522}}). k|Hiromitsu Ogawa}} was famous), but after succumbing to {{ill|Tsutsui Junkei|Q8192220|qid=Q8192220}} in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}}6 ({{ill|1578|Q6707|qid=Q6707}}), it declined and became discontinued in the same year ({{ill|1587|Q6744|qid=Q6744}}). From then on, it was under the exclusive jurisdiction of Daijo-in Temple throughout the Edo period, but this too was abolished in 1896.

=== Precincts ===
* Worship Hall - Built between 1829 and 1830. {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|de|Irimoya|es|Tejado de gabletes de Asia oriental|fr|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造|ko|팔작지붕|ru|Иримоя-дзукури|uk|Напіввальмовий дах|zh|歇山顶|qid=Q855025}}<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_03|title=Information about the worship hall/precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}</ref>.
*East and West Halls - Built over a period of approximately 12 years starting in 1828. Both halls are made of flowing Japanese cypress bark. Both shrines have a unique structure, with three Ikken-sha style shrines connected at the phase hall, and a single roof over which it becomes one hall of the five-ken shrine.<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=http://www.vill.higashiyoshino.nara.jp/tourism/unikawakamijinja|title=Nyukawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Higashiyoshino Village Hall}}</ref>.*Main shrine - Built over 12 years starting in 1828. Flowing cypress bark roof <ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_01|title=Guide to the main shrine/precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}</ref>.
:: The main shrine faces south, and the east and west shrines, where the deities are enshrined, are built on the left and right sides. The east and west halls are connected by a phase hall, and a stone staircase leads from the main hall to the worship hall.

* Stone lantern - A nationally designated important cultural property, stands in front of the east hall. It is 2.6 meters high and has an inscription on the pole that reads, ``Nyusha, 29th year of Kocho 22, carpenter I□□ client Uemon-jo'' (``22'' means ``4 years'') <ref>Masayoshi Kawakatsu, Dictionary of Japanese Stone Art (Tokyodo, 1978), p. 197</ref>. Although the □ part of the inscription is difficult to read, it is said to have been made by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Igyokichi}} in {{ill|Kōchō|Q1327323|qid=Q1327323}}4 ({{ill|1264|Q5514|qid=Q5514}}). Igyokichi is the son of the master craftsman {{ill|Igyosue|Q21652391|qid=Q21652391}}. His father, Igyosue, was in charge of stone work such as the restoration of Todaiji Temple, and Igyosue's family line is also known as the I-ha school, and is said to be a family of master craftsmen from the Kamakura period<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_04|title=Stone lantern (nationally designated important cultural property)/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}</ref>.* Granted Great Cedar - This is a large cedar tree that is approximately 1,000 years old, 51.5 meters tall, and has a trunk circumference of 7.3 meters.If you place your hands on the trunk and recite your wishes, you will be blessed with blessings.<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_05|title=Kanae-no-Osugi/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}</ref>.
* Stroking Owl - It is said to be an "owl" that has settled in Kanae Osugi, and is carved into an old mountain cherry tree that is about 200 years old.If you pet it, you will receive good luck.<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_10|title=Nyu no Nade Owl/Nyu Kawakami Shrine|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}</ref>.
* Aioi cedar - A large cedar tree that is about 800 years old and is also called a married couple cedar because of the two trees that stand straight up.<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_06|title=Aioi Cedar/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}</ref>.* Manai - Sacred water that flows from underground water flowing underground from the main shrine behind the main shrine into a well, and is said to bring good luck to the main enshrined deity, the Goddess of Water.<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_07|title=Nyu no Manai (purifying water)/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyu Kawakami Shrine}}</ref>.
* Tea room "Amanu" - {{ill|1969|Q2485|qid=Q2485}} (1969) A tea room connected to the shrine office by a breezeway<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_09|title=Tea room ``Amanu''/Guide to the grounds|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}</ref>.
* Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins - Excavation research has almost confirmed that the Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins are the Miyataki Ruins (Miyataki, Yoshino Town), but there is a theory that the sacred area of ​​Nyukawakami Shrine is the Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins. Therefore, in October 1966 (Showa 41), a monument commemorating the ``Historical Yoshino Imperial Villa Site'' was erected at the Higashiyoshino Village Local History Commemoration Society.<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_11|title=Yoshino Imperial Villa Ruins (Historic Site)/Guide to the Precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}</ref>.* Jiba Stone - Located next to the torii gate at the entrance to the west approach, it is said to have once been the gatepost of Yoshino Imperial Villa. Facing the torii gate, the left side is the old stone, and the right side is the old stone, also called the husband and wife stone.<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_12|title=Jijiba Stone/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}</ref>.
* Emperor Jinmu Sacred Monument - In {{ill|1940|Q18633|qid=Q18633}} (Showa 15), the Ministry of Education conducted the first survey of the sacred sites of Emperor Jimmu, and the sacred sites of Emperor Jimmu were designated as ``Land on the Nyu River.'' This area was identified as {{Sfn|Emperor Jimmu's sacred site|1942|pp=165-173}}, and a monument was erected at Kisayama, Hongumae (former shrine site) as the historic site of Hajimekuni. The sacred monument inscription reads, ``In order to bring peace to the world in September of the year 1999, Emperor Jinmu created the flat lotus and the gongon. It is engraved with the words, "The sacred shrine is near this place."* Yumebuchi - A place where three rivers, the Takami River, Hiragawa River, and Shigo River, meet to create a deep pool. In ancient times, the name Imibuchi was used as a sacred place where water gods were enshrined and where purification was performed, but it changed to ``Imebuchi'' and came to be called ``Yumebuchi.'' According to "Nihonshoki", it is said that during the time of Emperor Jimmu's Yamato pacification, Genren (a bottle containing sacred sake) was sunk into Yumebuchi at the upper part of the Nyu River to pray for victory, and victory was predicted by the flow of drunken fish large and small.At this time, the fish that floated on the water surface was called "Ayu", which is written as "Fish" and "Fortune".<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_14|title=Yumebuchi/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}</ref>.
* Himukashi Waterfall - Also called ``Akitsuno Waterfall'' and ``Ryujin Waterfall.'' It is located where the Hiragawa River joins the Takami River, and is said to be the home of the dragon god.As it is located east of the Yoshino Imperial Villa, it has come to be called the "East Falls"<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/keidai/#keidai_15|title=East Waterfall/Guide to the precincts|accessdate=2021-11-09|publisher=Niukawakami Shrine}}</ref>.
* Setsusha

=== Annual events ===
Main festivals <ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://niukawakami-jinja.jp/annual-events/|title=Festivals/Annual Events|accessdate=2021.11.9|publisher=Nyukawakami Shrine}}</ref>.
*January 16th - Suesha Mizu Shrine Festival
*April 16th - Suesha Kirai Shrine Annual Festival
*April 17th - Suesha Toshogu Shrine Festival
*June 4th - Water God Festival. People from companies involved in water, such as hydroelectric power generation and water supply projects, will be in attendance.
*July 16th - Setsusha Nyu Shrine annual festival.
*Second Sunday of October - Ogawa Festival (Taikodai Hosho Safety Prayer Festival) also known as the "Fighting Festival". Previously, it was held on {{ill|September 16 (Lunisolar)|Q840252|qid=Q840252|lt=September 16th of the lunar calendar}}, but it was changed in 1922. Also known as the ``Danjiri Festival,'' eight taiko drum stands are brought out from within the shrine ward and dance wildly around the shrine grounds. It is one of the three major festivals of Yamato.
*October 16th - Annual festival.

=== Cultural assets ===

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
* '''Stone lantern''' - Designated date: {{ill|1963|Q2755|qid=Q2755}} (1963) February 14th<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/6848|title=Stone lantern/Nationally designated cultural property database|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}</ref>.

=== Natural Monument (Nationally Designated) ===* '''{{ill|Niukawakaminakasha no Tsurumanryo jiseichi|Q121038166|qid=Q121038166}}''' - Designated date: {{ill|1957|Q5311|qid=Q5311}} (Showa 32) May 8th<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/1997|title=Nyukawakamichusha's natural habitat of the crane manryo/Nationally designated cultural properties database|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs}}</ref>. It grows in clusters on Mt. Komurodake behind the main shrine. {{ill|Evergreen forest|Q1024867|qid=Q1024867}} An evergreen stolonous shrub belonging to the family {{ill|Myrsinaceae|Q161260|qid=Q161260}} that grows on the bright forest floor of {{ill|Evergreen forest|Q1024867|qid=Q1024867}}. {{ill|Dioecy|Q148681|qid=Q148681}}. The stems grow straight at first and then slender. The long ones reach 1.5 meters, the flowers open around June-July, and the fruits become red-hot in late autumn-winter. It grows in clusters on semi-shady slopes in evergreen forests such as {{ill|Castanopsis|Q1065400|qid=Q1065400}} and {{ill|Cleyera japonica|Q775470|qid=Q775470}}. It succumbs to other weeds in bright, fertile areas, and declines in dark areas. Seedlings are rarely seen, and they are mainly propagated by stolons.

يىلى|uk|2018|ur|2018ء|uz|2018|vec|2018|vep|2018|vi|2018|vls|2018|vo|2018|wa|2018|war|2018|wuu|2018年|xmf|2018|yi|2018|za|2018 nienz|zea|2018|zgh|2018|zh|2018年|zh_classical|二〇一八年|zh_min_nan|2018 nî|zh_yue|2018年|zu|2018|qid=Q25291}} February 2, 2018<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://www.pref.nara.jp/secure/143530/kenshiteiichiran.pdf|title=List of cultural properties designated by Nara Prefecture|accessdate=2021-11-08|publisher=Nara Prefecture|page=13|format=PDF}}</ref>.
